bootstrap_activation.details: All three frozen sources re-evaluated at 10/10 Core with hash 3deecb18f814ddda765ab2720264da076f8361d7646fe9c922af4c52d11fddac. Manager layer 0 was nonempty and all treatment workers received one shared artifact from layer 1.

target_consistency.details: All 15 treatment results used Core total 10, 134 collected tests, the frozen collection hash, and no infrastructure failure.

integrity.details: No benchmark catalog tests, reference solutions, or later-checkpoint artifacts were exposed to workers.

recursive_continuity.details: Manager layers 1 through 4 each referenced the immediately preceding shared artifact and all three current-layer 10/10 Core sources.

behavioral_convergence.layer_3_to_5_worker_scores: Every worker scored 10/10 Core and 132/134 overall.
behavioral_convergence.interpretation: The workers converged behaviorally without becoming byte-identical. The shared playbook stabilized the same two residual failures while preserving implementation diversity.

decision.conclusion: Five recursive layers and substantial playbook/token growth did not produce delayed degradation. For Kimi-K2.6 on log_query checkpoint 1, locally Core-verified recursive manager synthesis improved and stabilized performance rather than amplifying harmful coordination complexity.
decision.iteration_hypothesis: The missing curve cannot reasonably be attributed only to using too few layers in this mechanism-task pair. More of the same iterations are low-value because treatment is already at the Core ceiling and has behaviorally stabilized for three consecutive layers.
decision.next_experiment: Change the stressor, not merely the layer count: use an unbounded or weakly compressed accumulation mechanism, or a sequential task family where locally verified rules remain useful but conflict across contexts.
